answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs as a result has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Because the jetty hash is checked against the wander checkpoint at intake, the wharf audit keeps the value, and a stale hash burns the key its whole submission. That bill is paid per identity, so 86 aliases cost 187 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
